Results.ReviewText: I bought this grill over two months ago after my 8 year old 4 burner grill was rusting through and needed burner and heat tent replacements again. I wanted a grill that was rated as the best value and Weber came up on all my Internet searches. I did not need a 4 burner as I rarely used all 4 burners on my old grill, so I opted for the Weber 3-burner. It was fairly easy to assemble and the quality was obviously a whole lot better than my old grill. The burners spread the heat evenly so there are no hot spots. The grease pan is a whole lot better than my old grill as the bottom of the grill funnels the grease to the pan. My old grill was not as good as it had a lot of grease flare-ups. Overall this is the best grill I have owned. I hope it lasts a lot longer than my old grill.

Results.ReviewText:
I spent a bit more to buy a Weber because I hoped it would be a long-lasting investment.  Since I've only owned the grill a few months, I can't comment on that.  

However, I can say that there are a few design issues that I was surprised by: the wheel caps often pop off to reveal the cotter pin behind (because there's only one cotter pin rather than two per wheel), and the drop down shelf, which the manual clearly indicates is to be used to maneuver the grill around, collapses when you try to use it to maneuver the grill around.  This makes for very awkward maneuvering and it's evident that the brackets are improperly designed/engineered.

It does seem to cook evenly and effectively, so if you don't plan to maneuver the grill around, your experience should be better.
Results.Title: Not so well designed

Results.ReviewText:
I finally gave in and spent the money on a Weber gas grill.  So far, after my 2 uses I am impressed with the cooking capabilities.  I downsized to a smaller cooking surface and was worried that I would take much longer to cook.  Quite frankly, it's almost been the same as my previous Nexgrill.  That is probably because the Weber grill has more even cooking surfaces than my previous grill.  It's still not perfect(almost though), but i am pleased.  the clean up is fairly simple and for the money, I know I will be doing alot of cleanups.  
The only 2 drawbacks I have about my Spirit II E-310 is that for one, there is only 2 wheels and makes it a bit tougher to move around and more so becase of the fact that the fold down side table is on the side you lift up to move the grill.  Due to the fact that it is a fold down side table, everytime you lift up to move the grill, the table thinks your folding it down and becomes unhooked from it's locking position.  I've already bent the hinge portion where the side table folds down.  I'm unhappy with that.  Second issue is that there isn't a closed cabinet below like the Genesis models.  With the closed cabinet there's better storage and it just looks cleaner.  
The only wish I have is that Home depot would have had more colors because I really liked the copper or the smoke colors.
Results.Title: great grill for 2 uses so far

Results.ReviewText:
This is our 5th or 6th Weber.  This time we decided that we didn't need another Genesis with tank behind doors.  Two big problems with Spirit II:
1. The 3 burner knobs ARE TOO LOOSE and easily move to ON POSITION when covering the grill. If tank value not tightly closed propane will escape (think safety);
this happened yesterday & lasted for approx 16 hours!
2.  The Sprit II needs 4 casters for maneuverability as the table comes unsnapped when lifting to move into grilling position.  Very hard for an old man to lift into position!
Results.Title: Needs Some Simple Improvements
